types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign nation-state with defined territory and government. Also called nation, state, sovereign. Examples: Spain, Netherlands, South Africa, Argentina.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are sovereign nations, matching schema.org Country.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: Tournament: A competition involving multiple teams or individuals, organized in a series of matches. Also called competition, championship, cup. Examples: World Cup, 2023 Women's World Cup, 2010 World Cup, 2026 World Cup.

chosen_type.label: SportsEvent
chosen_type.justification: World Cup editions are sports events; SportsEvent is the closest class.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: FootballTeam: An organized group of football (soccer) players representing a nation or club in competitions. Also called team, squad, side. Examples: Spain national football team, Spain women's national football team, La Roja, Spain's national team.

chosen_type.label: SportsTeam
chosen_type.justification: National football teams are sports teams.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, man, woman. Examples: King Felipe VI, Pedro Sanchez, Iker Casillas, Andres Iniesta.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

types.embedding_query_text: RoyalFamily: The members of a monarchy related by blood or marriage. Also called royal house, monarchy, dynasty. Examples: Spanish royal family, royal family.

chosen_type.label: RoyalFamily
chosen_type.definition: A family consisting of members of a monarchy related by blood or marriage.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class fits a royal family; mint as subclass of Thing.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

types.embedding_query_text: FootballPlayer: A professional athlete who plays football as a member of a football team. Also called player, footballer, soccer player. Examples: Ferran Torres, Rodri.

chosen_type.label: FootballPlayer
chosen_type.definition: A professional athlete who plays association football (soccer) at a competitive level.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches a football player; create new type under Thing.

candidates.label: UserPlays
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of playing media content. Also called user play, media playback, content viewing. Examples: a user playing a video, listening to an audio track, starting a game.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

candidates.label: GamePlayMode
candidates.comment: A GamePlayMode is an Enumeration indicating whether a game is multi-player, co-op, or single-player. Also called player mode, game type. Examples: SinglePlayer, MultiPlayer, CoOp.

types.embedding_query_text: Airline: A company that provides air transport services for passengers or cargo. Also called carrier, air carrier, airline company. Examples: Iberia.

chosen_type.label: Airline
chosen_type.justification: Mentioned entity is an airline company.

candidates.label: Airline
candidates.comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.

candidates.label: Flight
candidates.comment: A Flight is a Trip representing an airline journey. Also called air travel, plane ride, air route. Examples: Flight BA249 from London to Rio, a domestic flight from New York to Chicago, a charter flight.

candidates.label: TaxiService
candidates.comment: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. Also called cab company, taxi provider, ride-hailing service. Examples: 'Yellow Cab Co.', 'Uber', 'Lyft', a local taxi firm. Distinct from Taxi, which refers to an instance of the service or the vehicle itself.

candidates.label: FlightReservation
candidates.comment: A FlightReservation is a Reservation for air travel. Also called flight booking, airline reservation, plane ticket. Examples: A confirmed booking for a flight, a digital boarding pass, a reservation for a multi-leg journey. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tickets for sale.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

types.embedding_query_text: FootballClub: A football organization that fields a team, typically competing in domestic leagues. Also called club, soccer club, football organization. Examples: Manchester City.

chosen_type.label: SportsClub
chosen_type.justification: Manchester City is a football club, which fits SportsClub.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: HealthClub
candidates.comment: A HealthClub is a health and beauty local business providing facilities and services for physical fitness and wellness. Also called gym, fitness center, wellness club, athletic club. Examples: Gold's Gym, Planet Fitness, YMCA, a local yoga studio.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: ComedyClub
candidates.comment: A local business venue primarily dedicated to hosting comedy performances. Also called stand-up club, humor venue, comedy theater. Examples: The Comedy Store, Caroline's on Broadway, Second City, The Laugh Factory. Distinct from EntertainmentBusiness, which is a broader category for businesses providing entertainment.

types.embedding_query_text: Region: A geographic area that may be a state, province, or other sub‑national division. Also called province, state, area. Examples: New Jersey.

chosen_type.label: State
chosen_type.justification: New Jersey is a state, a specific kind of region.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

types.embedding_query_text: MediaOutlet: An organization that publishes news, articles, or other media content. Also called newspaper, press, media. Examples: Marca.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Marca is a news media organization.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
candidates.comment: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: MediaReviewItem
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an item or group of items treated as a single unit for evaluation within a MediaReview. Also called reviewed media unit, content item for review, media subject. Examples: a specific viral video, a collection of related images, a particular news clip.

types.embedding_query_text: Street: A public road in a city or town, typically with buildings on both sides. Also called road, avenue, boulevard. Examples: Calle de la Castellana, Castellana.

chosen_type.label: Street
chosen_type.definition: A public road in a city or town, typically with buildings on both sides.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches a street; mint under Place.

candidates.label: TaxiStand
candidates.comment: A civic structure or designated area where taxis wait for passengers. Also called cab stand, taxi rank, hack stand. Examples: a taxi stand at an airport, a designated taxi area outside a hotel, a street corner taxi queue.

candidates.label: Beach
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure consisting of a sandy or pebbly shore by a body of water. Also called seashore, coastline, sandy beach, waterfront. Examples: "Copacabana Beach", "Malibu Beach", "Waikiki Beach".

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.embedding_query_text: City: An urban settlement larger than a town, often serving as an administrative or economic centre. Also called municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: Madrid.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

types.embedding_query_text: Square: An open public space in a city, often surrounded by buildings. Also called plaza, public square, piazza. Examples: Cibeles Square, Cibeles square.

chosen_type.label: Square
chosen_type.definition: An open public space in a city, often surrounded by buildings.
chosen_type.justification: Square is not covered by existing classes; use CivicStructure as parent.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena

candidates.label: Park
candidates.comment: A Park is a civic structure or area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or protection of wildlife. Also called public park, green space, recreation area. Examples: Central Park in New York City, a local neighborhood park, a national park. Distinct from Garden, which is typically smaller and privately owned.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: PublicToilet
candidates.comment: A PublicToilet is a CivicStructure containing one or more toilets available for use by the general public, customers, or employees. Also called public restroom, public convenience, washroom. Examples: a toilet in a park, a restroom in a shopping mall, a public toilet facility at a train station, a highway rest stop bathroom.

types.embedding_query_text: Town: A human settlement larger than a village but smaller than a city. Also called small city, municipality, settlement. Examples: Ciudad Rodrigo.

chosen_type.definition: A human settlement larger than a village but smaller than a city.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A calendar day expressed in ISO‑8601 format. Also called day, calendar date, time point. Examples: 2026-07-16.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Mentioned value is a calendar date; matches schema.org Date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.
